title: PlantVillage Nuru identifies cassava disease symptoms at 65% accuracy against 40–58% for extension agents
summary: IITA-led evaluation in Kenya and Tanzania: the offline deep-learning app out-diagnosed extension officers (40–58%) and farmers (18–31%); six-leaf assessment raised accuracy to 74–88%.
account: Nuru is a deep-learning object-detection model inside the free PlantVillage Android app, trained on 2,756 cassava leaf images and able to run offline, developed by PlantVillage (Penn State) with FAO, IITA, CIMMYT and others. IITA researchers compared Nuru with cassava experts, agricultural extension officers and farmers at identifying cassava mosaic disease (CMD), cassava brown streak disease (CBSD) and cassava green mite damage, by inspecting plants in the field and by scoring a 170-image cassava symptom recognition assessment tool (CaSRAT) built from a farm in Mkuranga, Tanzania; CaSRAT was also used with 30 extension agents and 50 farmers from Busia County in western Kenya before and after they were introduced to the app. Nuru diagnosed cassava disease symptoms at 65% accuracy in 2020 versus 40–58% for extension agents and 18–31% for farmers, rising to 74–88% when six leaves per plant were assessed; mild symptoms were recognized at only 13–37%. Two weeks of practical use gave extension workers only a slight gain. No farm-level outcome is reported; the date used is the publication date.
purpose: Diagnose cassava mosaic disease, cassava brown streak disease and cassava green mite damage from leaf images on an offline Android phone.
system: PlantVillage Nuru cassava model (deep-learning object detection)
developer: PlantVillage, Pennsylvania State University, with FAO, IITA, CIMMYT and others
deployer: IITA field evaluation with extension officers and farmers in Busia County, Kenya, and in Tanzania
taxonomy_note: The paper also frames Nuru as an e-extension tool for transferring diagnostic knowledge, but the measured result is diagnostic accuracy.

ratings.reason: Farmers scored 18–31% on diagnosis; the paper reports only a “slight increase” in extension workers' skill after two weeks and no yield or income outcome.
No deployment outcome for extension services is documented beyond the accuracy comparison.

ai_role.statement: The study measures the model's diagnostic accuracy against humans; it does not document any alert that changed a management decision. Authors include the model's developers at IITA and Penn State, so the source is peer-reviewed rather than independent of the makers.

Field plants and a 170-image CaSRAT set scored by consensus of cassava experts
Comparison groups of 30 extension agents and 50 farmers from Busia County
must_hold: Symptoms expressed on the assessed leaves (mild symptoms were recognized at only 13–37%)
Six leaves per plant assessed to reach 74–88%

echoes.setting: Fall armyworm model in the same app, launched by FAO and Penn State

headline: PlantVillage Nuru out-diagnoses extension agents, 65% vs 40–58%
metric: 65% accuracy in 2020 versus 40–58% for extension agents and 18–31% for farmers

comparator.against: agricultural extension agents and farmers diagnosing the same cassava symptoms
comparator.quote: Nuru could diagnose symptoms of cassava diseases at a higher accuracy (65% in 2020) than the agricultural extension agents (40–58%) and farmers (18–31%).

later.note: A September 2024 study reports that the WAVE center has disseminated Nuru to cassava farmers in Côte d'Ivoire since 2020, with a 45% adoption rate among 152 respondents in three departments.
later.quote: In this regard, WAVE has been disseminating a plant disease detection smart application, “PlantVillage Nuru” to farmers since 2020.

claim_basis: One independent peer-reviewed study and the makers' peer-reviewed study are on file. There is no finding by a regulator or court.
